# manifold_threat_detection_rule (Resource)

Tunes one of Manifold's built-in threat detection rules. Rules can't be created or deleted, so this resource adopts an existing rule by id and manages only the attributes you set: `enabled` and `severity`. Leaving one out leaves it as it is.

Destroying the resource only removes it from state; the rule keeps its last tuning, because the API doesn't expose a rule's default settings to reset it to. Set the values you want back before destroying if that matters.

A rule's id can stop existing when Manifold renames or retires the rule. Refresh then drops it from state with a warning, and the plan fails rather than proposing a create that can't succeed: set `id` to the rule's current id from `manifold_threat_detection_rules`, or remove the resource.

Updates send the `ETag` from the last refresh as `If-Match`, so a rule retuned elsewhere after the plan was made fails the apply instead of being overwritten. Needs the `read:threats` and `write:threats` scopes.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "manifold_threat_detection_rule" "example" {
  id       = "EXAMPLE-001"
  severity = "critical"
}

# Switch off every rule mapped to a framework, without pasting their ids.
data "manifold_threat_detection_rules" "framework" {
  framework = "EXAMPLE-FRAMEWORK"
}

resource "manifold_threat_detection_rule" "framework" {
  for_each = { for r in data.manifold_threat_detection_rules.framework.rules : r.id => r }

  id      = each.key
  enabled = false
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `id` (String) The rule's identifier, as listed by `manifold_threat_detection_rules`. Changing it adopts a different rule.

### Optional

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the rule runs. Switching it off stops new threats; those it already raised stay.
- `severity` (String) Severity the rule's threats carry: `critical`, `high`, `medium` or `low`. A retune also applies to threats the rule already raised.

### Read-Only

- `category` (String)
- `created_at` (String) RFC 3339 creation timestamp.
- `description` (String) What the rule looks for, in one line.
- `owner` (String) Who maintains the rule.
- `taxonomy_mappings` (List of String) Framework codes the rule maps to, e.g. `OWASP-ASI02`.
- `title` (String)

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = manifold_threat_detection_rule.example
  id = "EXAMPLE-001"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Adopt a detection rule by its id.
terraform import manifold_threat_detection_rule.example EXAMPLE-001
```
